evals.name: discover-read-then-native-route
evals.prompt: A shared-repository owner must be asked for an integration window. Current runtime tool discovery has not yet returned. The executing agent proposes a single exec cell that prints ALL_TOOLS filtered by the current Codex namespace and immediately calls peer.py send. After the cell, discovery would show a native send_message_to_thread tool covering the exact known independent target. What should the agent do? No message has been sent; no installation or permission change is authorized.
evals.expected_output: Separate discovery from the dependent route decision, read the actual tool contract and target coverage, then use coord prepare -> the native tool with the exact prepared body -> coord commit. Do not preselect fallback, install a guard or grant mutation permission through a coordination reply.
expectations: Waits for and reads current discovery before choosing the sender; printing discovery and sending fallback in the same cell does not satisfy native-first
Uses the native tool when it covers the exact target, without also sending a script duplicate
Keeps coordination preparation and accepted/unknown/not_sent handling on the existing board contract
Makes no hook, receive-policy, service or authentication change

evals.name: accepted-fallback-is-not-replayed-after-discovery
evals.prompt: An agent prematurely used peer.py send while native discovery was still pending. The transport accepted the coordination, but receiver-side consumption is unverified. Discovery now returns a native tool covering that exact target. The user did not authorize a duplicate request. Describe recovery and the route for a future distinct coordination.
evals.expected_output: Retain the original message identity and accepted/unverified status, inspect its evidence through the applicable existing contract, and do not resend it through the newly discovered native tool. A future distinct coordination uses native prepare/send/commit after inspecting coverage.
expectations: Does not replay the same accepted or uncertain request through native transport
Distinguishes transport acceptance from consumption and business completion
Preserves the original message identity and does not delete queue state, resume a thread or change permissions
Uses native-first only for the future distinct request rather than retroactively duplicating this one
